newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN RENAULT WORKERS PROTEST AS CHIRAC VISITS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN RENAULT WORKERS PROTEST AS CHIRAC VISITS.

text.p: Workers from the doomed Belgian plant of French carmaker Renault noisily protested during Wednesday's start of a two-day visit by French president Jacques Chirac for talks with Belgian and EU leaders.
Police kept the workers from the car assembly plant at Vilvoorde, near Brussels, outside the section of the Brussels airport where official guests land.

In central Brussels where Chirac met Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene at the Egmont Palace, the 30-odd demonstrators, throwing firecrackers, were also kept at a distance during a brief protest. Riot police outnumbered protestors two to one.

Renault Vilvoorde union leader Karel Gacoms described February's closure decision by Renault, in which the French state still has a large equity stake, as "a brutal action." He added, "We have shown Chirac that we are still mobilised."
A banner in French read, "Renault Belgium: open for us and our children."
Dehaene was expected to discuss the closure, part of Renault plans to restore profitability and streamline operations, with Chirac. He has branded the plan "unacceptable."
Renault, however, has refused to back down.
Dehaene's interest in the fate of the workers reflects his general concern about unemployment in Belgium, but also the fact that the plant is in Vilvoorde, where he lives.
